newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobs rise could decide EMU target-Schaeuble.
newsitem.headline: German jobs rise could decide EMU target-Schaeuble.

text.p: Germany's drive to hit the deficit target for European monetary union could depend on a moderate shift in the country's average 1997 unemployment figure, the parliamentary chief of the ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) said in an interview.

A difference of 100,000 in the average unemployment count could lift tax revenue and ease jobless payments enough to enable Germany to meet the budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product, Wolfgang Schaeuble said in an article due to appear in the news magazine Der Spiegel on Monday.

"Whether we reach three percent depends in the end on the question whether the average unemployment is 100,000 higher or lower in the course of the year," Schaeuble said. "It's not much March's unadjusted unemployment count fell by 190,000 to 4.3 million, although independent economists said the fall did not mark a turnaround in the labour market.
Bonn has predicted a deficit ratio of 2.9 percent based on average unemployment of 4.2 million.
Schaeuble also repeated Bonn's firmness on EMU entry criteria. "We should stay with what we have always said: strict interpretation of the convergence criteria, especially the deficit," he said.
